info.title: media-service
info.description: Accepts video uploads, stores them on a shared Docker volume, and publishes a processing job to Redis for transcription-worker to pick up. Also serves the stored video with HTTP Range support for video players.

post.description:
Saves the uploaded file to the shared volume under `processed/{uuid}/video.mp4` (UUID path, not the original file name), then publishes a job to the Redis queue `sublio:job:queue` for transcription-worker. Returns immediately with 202 Accepted — this endpoint does not wait for processing to finish.

**Validation performed before the file is accepted:** - Content is verified by magic bytes, not by file extension or the
  client-supplied Content-Type (both are spoofable):
  - MP4: bytes 4–7 equal `ftyp`
  - MKV: starts with `0x1A 0x45 0xDF 0xA3`
  - AVI: starts with `RIFF`, bytes 8–11 equal `AVI `
- Files over 2GB are rejected. - Executable formats are rejected outright, regardless of extension:
  ELF, PE (Windows .exe/.dll), Mach-O.
- The original filename is never persisted — the file is always
  stored as `video.mp4` under a freshly generated UUID folder. This
  is a deliberate path-traversal protection: a crafted filename
  (e.g. `../../etc/passwd`) never reaches the filesystem layer.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: Client-supplied job identifier, correlated with the queued task.

video.description: The video file to upload. Validated server-side by magic bytes (MP4/MKV/AVI only); the original filename is discarded and is not used for storage. Maximum size 2GB.

202.description: File saved and job queued for processing. If this Idempotency-Key already exists (unique constraint), the original result is returned unchanged instead of saving the file and queuing a duplicate job. If the Redis queue is backed up beyond the configured depth, the upload is still accepted (202) — the client should watch the SSE progress stream for a "queued, position ~N" message rather than assume immediate processing. Processing itself is asynchronous either way; this response does not indicate completion.

400.description: Missing jobId, missing Idempotency-Key header, missing "video" field, or magic bytes did not match MP4/MKV/AVI

value.message: The jobId query parameter is required.
File content did not match MP4, MKV, or AVI magic bytes.

403.description: File identified as an executable format (ELF, PE, Mach-O) by magic bytes — rejected outright regardless of extension.

example.message: File identified as an executable format and was rejected.

500.description: Internal server error (e.g. Redis queue unavailable)

example.message: An unexpected error occurred while processing the upload.

get.description: Serves the file from `processed/{folderId}/{fileName}` on the shared volume. Supports HTTP Range requests so video players can seek without downloading the whole file.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description: UUID folder the video was stored under at upload time.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: File name within the folder (e.g. video.mp4).

200.description: Full file returned (no Range header was sent)

206.description: Partial content returned for the requested byte range

416.description: Range not satisfiable (e.g. start byte beyond file size). Accept-Ranges and Content-Range are still returned so the client knows the valid unit and total resource length.

500.description: Internal server error (e.g. file system unavailable)

example.message: An unexpected error occurred while serving the video.

AcceptRanges.description: Always "bytes" — advertises that Range requests are supported.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-generated UUID identifying this upload request, stored with a unique constraint. If a request arrives with an Idempotency-Key that was already used, the original upload result is returned unchanged (same 202, same jobId/folderId/fileName) instead of saving the file a second time — this is what makes a client retry after a network timeout safe. See backend/08-scalability.md.

folderId.description: UUID folder the video was stored under; used to build the playback URL.

ErrorResponse.description: Standardized error shape, identical across all Sublio services.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, e.g. MISSING_JOB_ID, MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY, MISSING_VIDEO_FIELD, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, EXECUTABLE_FORBIDDEN, FILE_TOO_LARGE, NOT_FOUND, RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.

traceId.description: Ties this error to a Tempo trace.
